title: Weeknight BBQ Ribs for the Crew
displayTitle: Weeknight BBQ Ribs for the Crew
seoTitle: Weeknight BBQ Ribs for the Crew | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Fast-finished ribs with a smoker shortcut
subtitle: Fast-finished ribs with a smoker shortcut
description: St. Louis ribs get a dry rub, smoke, and a covered finish before barbecue sauce is set.

steps.title: Heat smoker
steps.instruction: Preheat smoker to 275°F and stabilize the temperature before ribs go on.

steps.title: Remove membranes
steps.instruction: Pull the membrane from the bone side with a paper towel so rub can season both sides.

steps.title: Apply rub
steps.instruction: Coat ribs evenly with barbecue rub, pressing it on without making a thick paste.

steps.title: Smoke ribs
steps.instruction: Place racks bone-side down and smoke for 90 minutes, keeping the lid closed.

steps.title: Wrap racks
steps.instruction: Wrap each rack tightly with a splash of apple juice; loose foil leaks steam and dries ribs.

steps.title: Finish tender
steps.instruction: Return wrapped ribs to smoker until a toothpick slides between bones with little resistance.

steps.title: Check food safety
steps.instruction: Ribs are safe above 145°F, but tenderness usually arrives near 195°F; verify with a probe.

steps.title: Glaze ribs
steps.instruction: Unwrap carefully, brush with sauce, and smoke uncovered 10 minutes to set the glaze.

steps.title: Hold warm
steps.instruction: Cover ribs loosely and hold above 140°F; do not stack them tightly or the glaze smears.

steps.title: Cut and serve
steps.instruction: Slice between bones with a sharp knife and serve with potatoes and corn.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Pork ribs — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Pork ribs and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Choose similarly sized racks for even timing.
Do not rely on time alone; use the toothpick test.
Keep sauce warm for a smoother glaze.
tonightSpread: Condiments: barbecue sauce, pickles, hot sauce
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Pork ribs in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Pull remaining rib meat for fried rice.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The wrap phase protects tenderness and makes timing more reliable than an all-day rib cook.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: remove membranes and season ribs overnight. Storage: refrigerate cooked ribs for 3 days. Reheating: heat ribs to 165°F.
substitutions: Use baby back ribs for St. Louis ribs.
